newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian economy won't grow in 1997-deputy minister.
newsitem.headline: Russian economy won't grow in 1997-deputy minister.

text.p: The Russian economy will not grow in 1997, First Deputy Economy Minister Ivan Matyorov told the State Duma lower house of parliament on Tuesday.
"Towards the end of 1997, (gross domestic product) will be at the same level as 1996 -- that is, we will achieve zero growth," Matyorov told a parliamentary hearing.

He said exports, particularly raw materials including non-ferrous metals and chemicals, had helped bolster gross domestic product (GDP), but the budget crisis was the biggest threat to economic growth.

"Even talk about doubling the monetary base and the possibility of increasing yields on government securities by itself influences investors and shoots down the possibility of movement and return of (flight) capital," he said.

The government presented a bill to the Duma to slice 1997 budget spending by about one fifth. But some parliamentary leaders fiercely opposed the bill and suggested printing money to cover the budget deficit.
Matyorov said the budget cuts could restore some investor confidence and allow Russia to achieve zero or slight economic growth this year.
Forecasts earlier in the year predicted GDP growth of around two percent. The International Monetary Fund said last month it expected the Russian economy to grow by three percent this year.
